title: feat(audit): AI service accounts, O4 of ADR-0151 — principalKind reaches hooks and explain, so an account is attributed as itself
body:
repo:cloud#3 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbZqfEd7pcckjz3pGqn

Filing gate: **④ coordination — the open-code child of an accepted ADR.** ADR-0151 (card #31603, merged with PR #31615 as `cae8d8fe` on 2026-11-09) names this item **O4** under "What builds on this". Filed after that merge as the `repo:cloud#3` stand-down brief (#30278 comment 6727651596, item 3) owed; placement per the maintainer, verbatim there: 「objectstack 卡不用你派发，放到车道就行」 — triage routes it; the cloud seat does not dispatch it.

## What O4 is (ADR-0151 D5)
- Every audit writer (CRUD, action invocation, data export) records the account as `user_id` — which needs no change; pin it.
- `principalKind` reaches hooks and explain: today a hook learns an agent acted only from `performedByClientId`, which an account never carries. O4 surfaces the envelope's `principalKind` to hooks (the spec key is O4's to name), so the AI governance interceptor (O2) and approval routing (O6) ask one question for both kinds of agent.
- Refused by the ADR, not to be built here: a `performedBy` naming the account; any audit kind column (ADR-0118 D5); a per-write key id.

## Who reads this
Lane: triage routes it (`plugin-audit` + a `packages/spec` hook-context key ⇒ likely `domain:spec` for the key and `domain:server` for the writer; `domain:*` is triage's to set). It lands after #31739 (O3): the hook key needs no account, but its pins do. Consumers: O2, O6, cloud#3820's trace view.

Business reason: an Enterprise admin tracing what an AI did needs its writes attributed to the agent itself, and the governance seam needs to recognise both kinds of agent without a lookup.

Dedupe: same queries as the O3 card (no implementation card exists).
